title: The Big Show
paragraphs: NBC celebrity variety revue hosted by Tallulah Bankhead. Exact same-date RadioGOLDINdex records are matched by date and closest surviving duration.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Preserved first-season span (November 5, 1950 to May 6, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Preserved later-season span (September 30, 1951 to March 9, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Tallulah Bankhead (host and performer), Meredith Willson (music director), Meredith Willson and His Orchestra (performer), Dee Englebach (director and producer), Goodman Ace (performer and writer), Morton Green (writer), and Ed Herlihy (announcer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].
The stories often return to celebrity variety and revue, comedy and comic performance, popular music and orchestral performance, and Hollywood and Broadway celebrity culture.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes NBC prestige variety radio, Tallulah Bankhead as radio variety host, Network radio during television expansion, and Full-network and condensed rebroadcast preservation.
